availability_objective: Interactive work returns its first response within the explicit 30-second application-worker budget; streaming work yields bounded chunks; operator maintenance never runs through an HTTP request.

operations.demand: Parse at most 5 MiB and 10,000 rows, preview bounded data, then commit staged ledger entries transactionally.
operations.response_strategy: Use 64 KiB reads, reject immediately after a limit is crossed, and require release timing at the configured maximum; lower the limit or queue commits that approach 20 seconds.
operations.failure_and_retry: Close the upload in all paths, reject without retaining the file, and rely on submission tokens, row locks, and an atomic commit for safe retries.

operations.demand: Calculate payoff strategies and generate recurrence or pay-period occurrences.
operations.response_strategy: Reject horizons beyond fixed service limits and require timing and peak-memory evidence before increasing any limit.
operations.failure_and_retry: Validation errors return without persistence; generation writes run transactionally and lock the household boundary.

operations.demand: Render transaction, audit, import, and notification collections.
operations.response_strategy: Query only a fixed page or result slice; every new collection view must define a fixed result bound.
operations.failure_and_retry: Invalid page selectors resolve through Django's safe paginator behavior and ordinary GET requests are retryable.

operations.demand: Read and encode filtered transaction or protected audit histories.
bounds: one encoded CSV row yielded at a time
operations.response_strategy: Use StreamingHttpResponse and iterators so response construction and memory do not grow with the complete export; users narrow filters if a download is interrupted.
operations.failure_and_retry: An interrupted stream produces an incomplete download and no retained server artifact; the authorized user can retry a narrower export.

operations.demand: Perform password hashing, local blocklist lookup, MFA checks, and login-throttle updates.
bounds: fixed MFA token and clock-drift windows
five concurrent authenticated sessions per user
operations.response_strategy: Use local bounded data and fixed-cost checks; perform no password-derived network request and throttle repeated failures by identifier and network pseudonyms.
operations.failure_and_retry: Return generic authentication failures and a non-enumerating 429 boundary while retaining no candidate password or digest in logs.

operations.demand: Refresh household notifications, scrub stale staged imports, and archive security events.
operations.response_strategy: Use dedicated one-shot commands for routine generation and cleanup and a network-isolated collector for archival logging.
operations.failure_and_retry: Expose command failure through exit status and operational alerts; logging delivery failure emits a bounded redacted fallback without blocking the request.

operations.demand: Run database migration, encrypted backup or restore, key rotation, audit checkpoint, and recovery rehearsals.
bounds: bounded process trees and temporary filesystems
one operator-scheduled maintenance operation at a time
operations.response_strategy: Keep resource-intensive administration outside HTTP workers and serialize competing jobs on the private host.
operations.failure_and_retry: Stop on nonzero exit, preserve protected evidence or backup state, and retry only after resolving capacity or job-overlap conditions.

response_timeouts.purpose: Reject slow or stalled request headers.
Reject slow or stalled request bodies.
Terminate and replace a silent synchronous application worker.
Allow application timeout and worker replacement before ingress abandons the upstream.
Stop a response whose client is no longer consuming data.

residual_risks: Maximum-size CSV commit and worst-case projection timing still need representative release-host measurements.
A long-running streamed export can occupy one of the two synchronous web workers.
The conservative one-shot service ceilings still require representative release-host measurements and may need tightening.
